userStories.title: The shared fleet fixtures and fleet integration specs grant through bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert shared fleet fixture grants and all named fleet consumers together to preserve HTTP authorization outcomes on bindings alone.

**Motivation** — If drop-legacy carried that conversion as well, one branch would mix a schema drop with a rewrite of most of the integration suite, and a failing spec could not tell a lost grant from a real regression.

**Approach** — Changed symbols:
- `seedFleetBase` (`apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts`). Baseline: creates `User { role: 'ADMIN' }`. Target: creates the user with the default role, then `grantBaseline` and `grantRole(db, USER, 'admin', null)`.
- `seedFleetHttpWorld` (same file). Baseline: `prisma.projectMember.create` for dev (`DEVELOPER`) and viewer (`VIEWER`) on `web`. Target: `grantRole(prisma, USER, 'developer' | 'viewer', web.id)`, written before either user's first project request. Return shape unchanged.
- `seedFleetHttpAgent` (same file). Baseline: `POST /api/agents` with `roles: [...AGENT_ROLES]`, which writes four `AgentRoleEntry` rows. Target: the same request with `roles: []`; signature and return unchanged.
- `rosterFleetAgent(db, agentId, projectId)` (same file, new export). Grants the agent `viewer` plus `developer`, `reviewer`, `verifier` and `triager` in `projectId` through `grantRole`: exactly what a `seedFleetHttpAgent` agent with an `AgentProject` row in that project held before. The callers of `seedFleetHttpAgent` that write an `AgentProject` row call it instead.

Conventions carry over from retire-checks: PermissionsModule is global; project access refusal remains 403 projects and a refused key remains 403 permissions. Effective keys are cached, so direct binding writes after the principal's first permission check call MembershipService.invalidatePermissions before the next request. Helpers do not invalidate on their own. Keep every existing assertion and outcome, including production-no-legacy-row assertions; update stale legacy-fixture comments. Every directly Prisma-created user/agent gets grantBaseline immediately, not only the examples listed below. Agents posted as fixtures use roles:[]; bind each old role separately in every rostered project, never globally. Legacy ProjectMember roles map ADMIN -> project-admin, DEVELOPER -> developer, VIEWER/other -> viewer; AgentProject maps viewer; direct legacy USER ADMIN maps global admin and its User.role mirror.

The sentinel test: each listed spec adds one test named `fixtures grant through bindings only` calling `await expectBindingOnlyFixtures(db, principals, exempt);` with every user/agent created by its setup, including all seedFleetBase/seedFleetHttpWorld/seedFleetHttpAgent principals and outsiders. No exemptions are authorized for these fleet files. Place it as the first it after the describe's beforeAll fixture setup. A principal created only inside one test is not listed, but still receives its baseline. Clean is { legacyMemberships: 0, agentRoleEntries: 0, hasGlobalBinding: true, globalProjectRoleBindings: 0 }.

**Scope** — In: edit `apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts`, create `apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-fixtures-bindings.integration.spec.ts`, and convert exactly the following existing fleet specs (all paths below are under `apps/api/test/integration/fleet/`):
- `assistant-action-tools.integration.spec.ts` — writes a `ProjectMember` row (line ~92). The replacing invariant: a `developer` binding in `ops` through `grantRole`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-actions-approve.integration.spec.ts` — inserts a `ProjectMember` row (line ~208) and revokes it mid-test with `projectMember.deleteMany` (line ~194). The replacing invariant: a `developer` binding through `grantRole`; the revocation is `revokeProjectRoles` followed by `MembershipService.invalidatePermissions()`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-direct-action-record.integration.spec.ts` — creates its agent with `seedFleetHttpAgent` and writes an `AgentProject` row (lines ~45-46). The replacing invariant: `rosterFleetAgent` replaces the `AgentProject` write; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-direct-action.integration.spec.ts` — creates its agent with `seedFleetHttpAgent` and writes an `AgentProject` row (lines ~32-33). The replacing invariant: `rosterFleetAgent` replaces the `AgentProject` write; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-executor-caller.integration.spec.ts` — creates its agent with `seedFleetHttpAgent` and writes an `AgentProject` row (lines ~32-33). The replacing invariant: `rosterFleetAgent` replaces the `AgentProject` write; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-workspace-project-argument.integration.spec.ts` — `projectMember.createMany` (line ~55) and `deleteMany` (lines ~113, ~116), plus direct user creates. The replacing invariant: `developer` bindings through `grantRole`, removals through `revokeProjectRoles` plus `invalidatePermissions()`, `grantBaseline` for each created user; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-workspace-tools.integration.spec.ts` — writes a `ProjectMember` row without `await` (line ~53) and creates a user directly. The replacing invariant: an awaited `developer` binding and `grantBaseline`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-tool-executor.integration.spec.ts` — creates an outsider user directly (line ~56) that relies on the baseline fallback. The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline` for it; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `assistant-actions-decide.integration.spec.ts` — promotes the viewer with `projectMember.updateMany({ role: 'ADMIN' })` (line ~86). The replacing invariant: `revokeProjectRoles` + `grantRole(..., 'project-admin', web)` + `invalidatePermissions()`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.

- `permissions-workspace-threads.integration.spec.ts` — `agentProject.createMany` (line ~104). The replacing invariant: one `viewer` binding per rostered project and `grantBaseline`; the legacy-absence assertions at lines ~219 and ~231 stay; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `workspace-create.integration.spec.ts` — `projectMember` upsert, update, deleteMany and createMany for dev and root (lines ~30-58); AC-10 relies on root having no membership in `web`. The replacing invariant: each write becomes `grantRole` / `revokeProjectRoles` with the mapped key plus `invalidatePermissions()` where a request already ran; root keeps its global `owner` binding from registration, so AC-10 is decided by its project bindings as before; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.

Specs that use `seedFleetHttpAgent` but roster the agent in no project (`fleet-analytics-api`, `fleet-dashboard-api`, `thread-content-events`, `thread-creator-type`, `workspace-read`) are not edited: the helper's `roles: []` changes nothing for them, because the roles applied in no project.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing seedFleetBase, seedFleetHttpWorld and seedFleetHttpAgent signatures and return shapes. Add `rosterFleetAgent(db, agentId, projectId)` as specified above; consume the US-001 `grantBaseline`, `grantRole`, `revokeProjectRoles`, `fixtureGrantReport` and `expectBindingOnlyFixtures` interfaces without changing them. Prove the helper-to-HTTP seam with the real tickets route and project-isolated effective keys.

userStories.title: Permission integration specs grant through bindings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert the named permissions integration fixtures to explicit baseline and scoped role bindings without altering their existing authorization assertions.

**Motivation** — After this feature, a converted spec passes only on bindings, and drop-legacy can remove the union without touching these specs.

**Approach** — Effective keys are cached (`PermissionCache`), so a spec that writes or deletes a binding directly **after** the principal's first permission check calls `MembershipService.invalidatePermissions()` before the next request, as the enforce-* suites already do. A grant written before the principal's first request needs no invalidation.

**Assertions stay; stale comments do not.** Comments that describe a converted fixture as legacy rows (for example "roster row and legacy roles") are updated with it. A converted spec keeps every existing assertion and its outcome. Only fixture setup, mid-test grant changes and the new sentinel test change. Where a spec asserts that production wrote **no** legacy row (for example `prisma.agentProject.count(...)` equal to 0 after an API call), that assertion stays: it pins production behaviour drop-legacy removes.

**Every principal a converted spec creates is covered.** A converted spec gives **every** user and agent it creates through Prisma its baseline with `grantBaseline`, and converts **every** legacy grant it writes, not only the ones its Modifies entry names as examples. A principal is exempt only where its Modifies entry says so, because the spec asserts that principal's exact bindings.

**Agents created through `POST /api/agents` as fixtures carry no roles.** Production still writes an `AgentRoleEntry` per `roles` item on that route, and the union reads those rows as project roles. A fixture agent is created with `roles: []` and gets each role as a project binding (conversion table). An agent whose `roles` the spec asserts in an API response (the agent API is the subject) keeps them, and its sentinel exempts its `AgentRoleEntry` rows; its access grants still convert.

Map ProjectMember ADMIN/DEVELOPER/VIEWER-or-other to project-admin/developer/viewer in the same project. AgentProject becomes viewer; AgentRoleEntry DEVELOPER/REVIEWER/VERIFIER/TRIAGER becomes developer/reviewer/verifier/triager in each rostered project, never globally. Legacy global USER ADMIN becomes a global admin binding through grantRole, which also mirrors User.role. Direct role changes/removals use revokeProjectRoles (+ grantRole for replacement), then invalidatePermissions.

Each listed spec gains one test named `fixtures grant through bindings only` calling `await expectBindingOnlyFixtures(db, principals, exempt);` as the first it after its beforeAll setup. Include every setup user/agent, including outsiders; single-test-local principals still get baselines but are not listed in that setup sentinel. Clean means {legacyMemberships:0, agentRoleEntries:0, hasGlobalBinding:true, globalProjectRoleBindings:0}. Only globalBind in membership-notification-consumers is exempt under globalProjectRoles; no noBaseline or agentRoleEntries exemptions are authorized here.

**Scope** — In: edit only these files under `apps/api/test/integration/permissions/`:
- `core-comments-labels-watchers.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes an `AgentProject` row (line ~139). The replacing invariant: the agent is created, gets `grantBaseline` and a `viewer` binding in the project; a `fixtures grant through bindings only` test asserts the sentinel report for every fixture principal; all existing outcomes unchanged.
- `core-ticket-links.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes an `AgentProject` row and an `AgentRoleEntry` `DEVELOPER` (lines ~143-144). The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, then `viewer` and `developer` bindings in the fixture project (never global); sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `core-ticket-routes.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes an `AgentProject` row and an `AgentRoleEntry` of a parameterised role (lines ~121-122). The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, `viewer`, and a binding of the mapped role key in the fixture project; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `core-ticket-transitions.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes `AgentProject` + `AgentRoleEntry` (lines ~113-114). The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, `viewer` and the mapped role key bound in the fixture project; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `enforce-fleet-approvals-budgets.integration.spec.ts` — its `createAgent(slug, roles)` posts the given `roles` to POST /api/agents and writes an `AgentProject` row in `p1` (lines ~117-120); `p1-approval-dev-agent` is created with `['DEVELOPER']` (line ~251). The replacing invariant: `createAgent` sends `roles: []`, then grants `viewer` in `p1` and a binding of each mapped role key in `p1` (so `p1-approval-dev-agent` gets `viewer` and `developer`); sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `enforce-fleet-config-knowledge.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes `AgentProject` + `AgentRoleEntry` (lines ~113-114). The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, `viewer` and the mapped role key in the project; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.

The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, `viewer` and the mapped role key in the project; sentinel test added; the legacy-absence assertions at lines ~268, ~322 and ~360 stay; outcomes unchanged.
- `enforce-fleet-jobs.integration.spec.ts` — its agent fixture writes `AgentProject` + `AgentRoleEntry` (lines ~93-94). The replacing invariant: `grantBaseline`, `viewer` and the mapped role key in the project; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged. Add a second project p2 to observe that the developer agent's ticket.create key does not leak outside p1.

- `enforce-fleet-schedules.integration.spec.ts` — its `createAgent` sends POST /api/agents with `roles: ['DEVELOPER']` and writes an `AgentProject` row in `p1` (lines ~101-103). The replacing invariant: `roles: []`, then `viewer` and `developer` bindings in `p1` through `grantRole`, before the existing `invalidatePermissions()`; sentinel test added; the legacy-absence assertions at lines ~181 and ~281 stay; outcomes unchanged.
- `enforce-fleet-requesters.integration.spec.ts` — it creates a `User { role: 'ADMIN' }` (line ~110) and an agent through `prisma.agent.create` (line ~112). The replacing invariant: the user is created with the default role and gets `grantBaseline` plus a global `admin` binding; the agent gets `grantBaseline`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.

The replacing invariant: the ADMIN users get `grantBaseline` plus a global `admin` binding (which mirrors `User.role`), every other created user gets `grantBaseline`; the sentinel exempts the `globalBind` user under `globalProjectRoles`; the `User.role` assertion at line ~174 stays; outcomes unchanged.
- `core-seeded-roles.integration.spec.ts` — it creates users through Prisma (line ~35) that rely on the baseline fallback. The replacing invariant: each created user gets `grantBaseline`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
- `enforce-fleet-foundations.integration.spec.ts` — it creates users through Prisma (line ~35) that rely on the baseline fallback. The replacing invariant: each created user gets `grantBaseline`; sentinel test added; outcomes unchanged.
Out: US-001 owns helper creation; shared fleet changes are US-002; remaining integration consumers are US-004; e2e/seed are US-005; unit doubles are US-006. **Goal** — Convert the named non-fleet/non-permissions integration fixtures to bindings and explicit baselines while preserving domain outcomes and narrowly intentional exact-binding fixtures.

**Every principal a converted spec creates is covered.** A converted spec gives **every** user and agent it creates through Prisma its baseline with `grantBaseline`, and converts **every** legacy grant it writes, not only the ones its Modifies entry names as examples. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace legacy-state authorization decisions in the four named unit doubles/cases with explicit held-key or binding authority.

**Motivation** — Converting the fixtures first, while the union still answers, keeps both features reviewable.

**Approach** — The unit doubles (US-006):

| Spec | Today | After |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `apps/api/src/projects/project-membership.guard.spec.ts` | the `can` double answers the global `project.read` ask with `principal.role === 'ADMIN'` | it answers from a `globalReaders: Set<string>` of principal ids; AC4's global reader is a `role: 'MEMBER'` user in the set |
| `apps/api/src/projects/project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts` | same | same; AC4's caller is a `role: 'MEMBER'` user in `globalReaders` |
| `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.spec.ts` | AC-7 "a global ADMIN creator" sets `creator: { role: 'ADMIN' }` | the creator has `role: 'MEMBER'`; `access.resolveMembership` resolving `'ADMIN'` (the display role of a global reader) admits it |
| `apps/api/src/permissions/role-admin.service.spec.ts` | AC-22 gives `grantor-2` its global authority with `addUser('grantor-2', 'ADMIN')` | `addUser('grantor-2')` plus `store.bind({ type: 'USER', id: 'grantor-2' }, 'admin')` |

`InMemoryPermissionStore.addUser(id, role)` keeps its `role` parameter: the compat unit specs use it.

Detailed replacing invariants:
- `apps/api/src/projects/project-membership.guard.spec.ts` — the `can` double answers the global `project.read` ask with `principal.role === 'ADMIN'` (lines ~149-151), and AC4 builds its global reader as a `role: 'ADMIN'` principal. The replacing invariant: the double answers the global ask from a `globalReaders` set of principal ids; AC4's principal has `role: 'MEMBER'` and is in the set; every other case keeps its outcome. Also prove that an ADMIN claim alone outside globalReaders is refused by the global ask.
- `apps/api/src/projects/project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts` — the same double (line ~134) and the same AC4. The replacing invariant: the same `globalReaders` set; AC4's caller has `role: 'MEMBER'` and is in the set; every other case keeps its status.
- `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.executor.spec.ts` — AC-7 (lines ~184-187) is "a global ADMIN creator" built from `creator: { role: 'ADMIN' }`. The replacing invariant: the creator has `role: 'MEMBER'`, `access.resolveMembership` resolves `'ADMIN'`, the tool runs, and the `resolveMembership` call assertion matches `role: 'MEMBER'`; the title names the global reader, not the claim.
- `apps/api/src/permissions/role-admin.service.spec.ts` — AC-22 (line ~733) gives `grantor-2` global authority with `addUser('grantor-2', 'ADMIN')`. The replacing invariant: `addUser('grantor-2')` plus `store.bind({ type: 'USER', id: 'grantor-2' }, 'admin')`; the outcome is unchanged. Keep the existing superuser binding and last-owner refusal with permissions.ownerLocked, not a new escalation refusal. Update the comment that currently describes legacy ADMIN as the authority source.

**Scope** — In: only the four unit specs above, with existing outcomes/statuses and other assertions preserved. Out: DB fixture conversion and sentinel helpers are US-001 through US-005. Do not edit production services, InMemoryPermissionStore.addUser's signature, legacy subject cases, membership.service.spec.ts's disabled ADMIN case, projects-find-all-for-principal.spec.ts's unreachable legacy branch or tickets.service.spec.ts's claim-only stubs.

**Interface** — Use existing `InMemoryPermissionStore.bind(principal, roleKey, projectId?)` with `{ type: 'USER', id: 'grantor-2' }` and `'admin'` globally. The guard double's global ask for PROJECT_ACCESS_KEY='project.read' consults `globalReaders: Set<string>`; project-specific asks retain existing refusal modeling. ProjectAccessService.resolveMembership's `'ADMIN'` result is a display role, not an authorization decision based on the caller's claim. No new source helper or public interface is introduced.

analysis:
Goal and migration boundary: this is permissions P1i, the ninth P1 feature, after roles, membership, enforce-core, enforce-fleet, enforce-assistant, enforce-integrations, contract-tests and retire-checks. Convert test access grants and baseline setup while the legacy union remains available, separating fixture regressions from the subsequent schema/union removal. No production authorization change, schema migration, OpenAPI regeneration, client change, dependency change or union-disable switch belongs here. The feature has exactly six stories, all in apps/api, with the binding dependency graph specified below. The introductory reference to five unit specs is inconsistent with the explicit unit-double table and US-006 Modifies list: implement exactly the four named unit files. The Seams paragraph refers to US-001 AC 12 as PermissionService integration proof, but the actual authoritative criterion is US-001 AC 14; AC 12 is the sentinel exemption check.

Discovery and architecture: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this tool session, so structural discovery used direct reads and text searches. The supplied automatic Express/Next.js labels are not authoritative: API guidance specifies NestJS 12 + Fastify and the web is Nuxt (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:23; root repository guidance). apps/api/test/helpers/http-app.ts:26-44 boots AppFactory, installs CombinedAuthGuard and the real prefix/pipes/filters/guards, and initializes the app. Use this existing real-HTTP harness rather than creating an alternate authorization stack. apps/api/package.json:11-34 defines Vitest test/test:scoped/test:integration and seed:e2e; apps/api/vitest.config.ts:5-14 configures SWC with decorator metadata and :16-18 selects DB mode/globs. Unit tests live beside src; new DB behavior specs belong in test/integration. Read the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before any NestJS implementation; it was not needed to author this PRD and was not exposed in this session.

US-001 findings: apps/api/src/permissions/system-role.seeder.ts:25-33 accepts the seed list and RoleRepository and validates all seeds before sequential writes. :40-50 calls only findOne({ key }), createRole and update; :53-64 supplies seed defaults system=true and locked=false; :71-85 restores locked-role permissions/name/scope but preserves unlocked-role permission edits. Therefore ensureSystemRoles must reuse this production seeder through a small db.role adapter, with the prescribed RoleRepository cast, not copy the seed logic. apps/api/src/permissions/system-roles.ts:17-174 defines exactly eleven seeds: four GLOBAL roles owner/admin/member/agent and seven PROJECT roles project-admin/developer/reviewer/verifier/triager/approver/viewer. Compare optional system/locked fields using their production defaults. apps/api/src/permissions/permissions.types.ts:20-29 defines RoleDomain with permissions:string[] whereas schema Role.permissions is Json (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1571-1584), so the adapter must respect the domain/Prisma boundary. PrincipalRef is type USER|AGENT plus id (permissions.types.ts:74). apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1587-1603 shows polymorphic principalId has no foreign key, role deletion is restricted and project deletion cascades. Two partial unique indexes, not a Prisma composite unique selector, enforce nullable-global/project binding identity (apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts:13-14). Idempotent grant lookup must include principalType, principalId, roleId and normalized projectId; null/omitted global arguments must not create duplicate bindings. If reporting a nonexistent principal, explicitly satisfy the all-zero/no-global failure contract rather than treating orphan polymorphic bindings as evidence of a real actor. Helpers take only the generated PrismaClient or PrismaService.client, never Nest DI or MembershipService. Grants record SYSTEM/test and seed roles lazily when their key is absent; unknown keys must create no binding. apps/api/test/helpers/reset-db.ts:24-35 truncates every application table, including Role, so no process-level seeded flag may survive resetDb.

Permission and cache seam: apps/api/src/permissions/permission.service.ts:87-94 caches effective keys by principal and scope; :121-160 computes the union of bindings, legacy rows and baseline fallback, including legacy-admin elevation. Do not edit this service. apps/api/src/permissions/membership.service.ts:85-95 provides invalidatePermissions; :110-114 establishes production member/agent baselines; :116-120 sends global-admin grants through createBinding. :40-50 documents the global owner/admin User.role mirror and token/cache behavior. The fixture copies only the required User.role='ADMIN' mirror for USER global owner/admin bindings, not production token revocation behavior. The helper itself never invalidates permission caches. A spec writing or deleting bindings directly after its principal's first permission check must call MembershipService.invalidatePermissions before the next request; grants before first permission use need none. An awaited mirror before login avoids stale JWT claims. apps/api/src/projects/project-access.service.ts:45-62 decides project access using project.read, distinguishes a global reader from project display membership, and is a read-only source of truth.

US-002 impact: apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts:19-27 creates the legacy ADMIN fixture; :60-90 creates the real HTTP world and inserts ProjectMember rows at :76; :95-104 posts all AGENT_ROLES, creating legacy role entries. Replace those grants together with all named fleet consumers because several consumers update/delete the very rows the helper currently creates. Preserve every existing export signature and return shape. Add rosterFleetAgent to reproduce viewer plus all four agent roles, scoped to each rostered project, never globally. Helper users created through production API already receive baselines; seedFleetBase's directly created admin needs one explicitly. Existing importers beyond the converted list benefit without file edits; do not broaden to helper-only consumers whose unrostered agents have no project role applicability. Concrete cache-sensitive cases were verified in assistant-actions-approve.integration.spec.ts:192-210 (revoke/restore in try/finally) and workspace-turns.integration.spec.ts:66-81 (viewer/null lost-hosting test and restore). Preserve their status, message, side-effect and action-state assertions.

US-003 impact: enforce-fleet-jobs.integration.spec.ts:89-99 creates legacy roster/role rows and already invalidates permissions; its header :1-10 describes the legacy setup and must change with the fixture. Preserve real HTTP role-matrix outcomes while moving each agent's viewer and role grants into p1, and add p2 negative isolation. membership-notification-consumers.integration.spec.ts:63-68 directly creates users with a requested legacy role, :76-98 filters PROJECT-scope sources in its assertion helpers, and :144-153 intentionally creates a global viewer. Baselines/admin GLOBAL-scope bindings therefore do not violate its existing PROJECT-source assertions. Preserve the admin role assertion at :174, deliberately exempt only globalBind for globalProjectRoles, and retain that binding as the subject under test. Existing MembershipService binding writes are not legacy grants and need not be replaced indiscriminately.

US-004 impact: home-api.integration.spec.ts:59 uses seedFleetHttpWorld and :92-95 nests a ProjectMember create inside a soft-deleted project; replace only the nested fixture with a project-admin binding and leave home outcomes intact. Its final test creates an agent locally (:134-137): it still gets production baseline but is not listed in the beforeAll sentinel. project-membership-gate.integration.spec.ts:238-252 posts DEVELOPER and creates an agent roster in team and other; grant viewer+developer in both and preserve legacy-absence assertions. notification-eligibility.ts:30-50 still reads User.role for global admin eligibility and principalIdsWithAccess for project sources, explaining the required mirror; this production reader stays unchanged. vcs-webhook-secret.integration.spec.ts:53-78 creates unrostered hook-agent and deliberately deletes both binding agents' full binding sets before writing one exact project grant. Preserve those exact-binding premises and exempt only those two under noBaseline. auth/disabled-user.integration.spec.ts:27-29 creates a setup user, and :52-54 creates another inside a single test: both need grantBaseline, but only the setup user belongs in the setup sentinel. Apply this distinction to all named files, not only examples.

US-005 impact: prisma/seed-e2e.ts:10-16 currently constructs PrismaClient at import time and logs the initial message; :18-35 wipes tables but omits RoleBinding; :39-53 grants ADMIN via a user field and ProjectMember; :60-68 logs completion and exits/disconnects. Move data work into import-safe seed-e2e-data.ts exporting seedE2e(db), delete RoleBinding before users (polymorphic ids do not cascade), create admin with default role, and grant member/admin globally plus project-admin on fleet-e2e. Keep project/repo/password and both messages unchanged, and create/disconnect the client inside the thin runner's main lifecycle using createPgAdapter. Do not use import.meta.main under CommonJS. Real seed rerun and login/GET checks cover dangling bindings, restore behavior and API boot compatibility. agents.e2e.spec.ts:31-83 creates users in setup, :58 updates ADMIN, and :89-112 creates the API-subject agent and roster. Keep its asserted roles; sentinel must run immediately before deletion, not as the first initial test. api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts is a 4,995-line sequential lifecycle suite; :297 creates the only role-asserted agent and :333 asserts roles. Preserve all original assertions and outcomes, track surviving fixture actors without adding inside-test-only principals to a setup sentinel, run its sentinel last and omit deleted temp-agent. Do not pre-grant roster-route subjects or break the existing 409 already-assigned case.

US-006 impact: project-membership.guard.spec.ts:140-154 and project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts:126-140 authorize global project.read from principal.role, although production already uses keys. Replace those branches with globalReaders sets, reset state at the appropriate lifecycle, model the positive global reader with MEMBER and verify a bare ADMIN claim is refused by the global ask. assistant-tool.executor.spec.ts:184-188 names/globalizes an ADMIN claim; keep the resolved display role ADMIN but make the creator claim MEMBER. role-admin.service.spec.ts:718-744 gives grantor-2 legacy ADMIN plus superuser to reach permissions.ownerLocked. Replace only that authority source with an explicit global admin binding and update the legacy comment; retain superuser and last-owner refusal assertions. InMemoryPermissionStore.addUser's optional legacy role remains for compat users (in-memory-permissions.ts:40-42); bind already records SYSTEM/test and normalizes its default global projectId (:50-63). Production/test-helper shared implementation stays unchanged except the new fixture module.

Shared conversion design, binding on all consuming stories: ProjectMember ADMIN -> project-admin; DEVELOPER -> developer; VIEWER or any other stored value -> viewer, all in the same project. AgentProject -> project viewer. Each AgentRoleEntry DEVELOPER/REVIEWER/VERIFIER/TRIAGER -> developer/reviewer/verifier/triager in every project where that fixture agent was rostered, never a global PROJECT-role binding. Fixture POST /api/agents sends roles:[] and receives the same per-project bindings; an unrostered fixture gets no project role grant. The two API-subject role-asserting agents retain rows with narrowly named agentRoleEntries exemptions, but their access grants still convert. Any legacy User ADMIN grant -> global admin through grantRole, maintaining the mirror. Mid-test role replacement -> revokeProjectRoles then grantRole then invalidation; removal -> revokeProjectRoles then invalidation; restoration invalidates too. Every directly Prisma-created permission participant, including outsiders and locally created test-only actors, gets grantBaseline immediately after creation unless its Modifies entry expressly exempts exact bindings.

Sentinel contract and placement: clean means {legacyMemberships:0, agentRoleEntries:0, hasGlobalBinding:true, globalProjectRoleBindings:0}. Every listed converted spec (not the shared helper/seed runner/data module) adds one test named fixtures grant through bindings only calling expectBindingOnlyFixtures for all users/agents from the relevant fixture setup, including seedFleetBase/world/agent principals and refused outsiders. Put it first after the describe's beforeAll fixture setup. Single-test-created principals still get baseline but are not retroactively listed. Only exemptions: membership-notification-consumers.globalBind under globalProjectRoles; vcs binding-admin-agent and binding-developer-agent under noBaseline; agents/API endpoint role-asserted main agent under agentRoleEntries. Exemptions are keyed by principal type and id and suppress only their designated field, never unrelated legacy memberships. Sentinel errors aggregate each failing id and field into one Error. Mirrored USER ADMIN (global owner/admin plus User.role) is clean, unmirrored ADMIN adds one legacyMemberships. Keep existing production-no-legacy-row assertions and every existing outcome; update stale setup comments only.

Execution and verification notes: use generated Prisma imports from src/generated/prisma/client, tests' createTestPrismaClient, and createPgAdapter for the script; never @prisma/client imports. DB tests must actually execute with KODA_DB_TESTS=1 via bun run test:scoped or the configured acceptance command, not pass as describe.skip. Bring compose test Postgres up with bun run test:db:up outside a sandbox without Docker; DB global setup selects dedicated test database or Testcontainers, never inherited production DATABASE_URL. Existing DB/e2e assertions plus binding-only sentinels prove grant provenance without disabling the union; drop-legacy remains the final proof. There is no manual rules-document edit in this run.
